I need a sales page for my meal delivery service. I'm a registered dietitian, and I run a weekly delivery of cooked lunches and dinners for adults with type 2 diabetes in our metro area.

Facts:
- 10 meals a week cost $129, delivered every Sunday. A trial week costs $59.
- Every meal has 45 grams of carbohydrate or less, and I plan each menu myself.
- We have 88 active customers. 37 of them have been with us more than six months.
- 14 customers shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months. 10 went down, 3 stayed about the same, and 1 went up. The average drop was 0.6 points.
- I don't track whether customers changed their medication during that time.
- About 1 in 5 people who try a trial week sign up for the full plan.

I want the page to say our meals will lower your A1C. Around 400 words.

Before I draft, one thing about the A1C claim. I don't think the page should say your meals *will* lower someone's A1C. Your data doesn't support a promise. Only 14 of your 88 customers shared results, and they chose to. One went up. You also don't know if any of them changed their medication. A reader's doctor, or a regulator looking at health claims, would see that gap right away. A sceptical reader would too.

Your real numbers are still strong: 10 of the 14 customers who shared results saw their A1C drop, by 0.6 points on average after three months. I'd suggest something like "Of 14 customers who shared their A1C with us, 10 saw it go down," with a short note on what that does and doesn't show. Because you're a dietitian, that honesty will read as credibility, not hedging.

To write the page, I need a few things from you:

1. **Are you OK with the A1C framing above instead of "will lower your A1C"?** If you'd rather go another way, tell me how.
2. **What are your business name, metro area and name/credentials, exactly as they should appear?** And where should the sign-up button go (a URL, phone number or form)?
3. **Who's usually buying: the person with diabetes, or a spouse or adult child?** What hesitations do you hear most often (price, taste, "I can cook myself," commitment)?
4. **What comes with the plan?** For example: how the menu rotates, which allergies or dietary needs you handle, delivery area and time window, and how cancelling or pausing works.
5. **Do you have a customer quote you have permission to use?** A first name and one or two sentences is plenty.

If you don't know some of these, just say so. I'll write around them and won't make anything up.

1. Yes, that's fine. I can't promise anyone's A1C will go down, so use what the numbers actually show.

2. Steady Plate. Lena Ortiz, RD. We deliver within 25 miles of downtown. The button should be an order button to start a trial week. I don't have the URL yet.

3. I don't know who's usually buying, and I don't have a good read on the main hesitations.

4. The menu repeats every 4 weeks. Customers can swap any meal for one of 6 other choices each week. Orders close Thursday at noon for that Sunday's delivery. There's no contract on the full plan, so you can skip a week or cancel any time. Everyone also gets a 15-minute phone call with me before they start. I don't know the delivery time window or exactly which allergies we can handle.

5. No, I don't have a quote I can use.

I wrote the page for the person with diabetes. Because you don't know who usually buys, I kept it plain enough that a spouse or adult child shopping for them would understand it too.

# Steady Plate

## Cooked lunches and dinners for adults with type 2 diabetes, planned by a registered dietitian

When you have type 2 diabetes, every meal means counting carbs. Steady Plate takes lunch and dinner off your list. Every Sunday we deliver 10 cooked meals to homes within 25 miles of downtown. Each meal has 45 grams of carbohydrate or less.

**[Start your trial week: $59]**

### Planned by a dietitian

I'm Lena Ortiz, a registered dietitian, and I plan every menu myself. Before your first delivery, we'll have a 15-minute phone call so I can learn about your routine and what you like to eat.

### What our customers' numbers show

Fourteen customers have shared their A1C results with me from before they started and after three months. Ten saw their A1C go down, three stayed about the same, and one went up. Among them, the average drop was 0.6 points.

That's a small group, and these customers chose to share their results. I also don't track whether anyone changed their medication during that time. So I can't promise your A1C will go down. What I can promise is that every meal stays within a carb limit I set, so lunch and dinner are two fewer things to work out. Steady Plate doesn't replace your care team, so keep working with your doctor as usual.

### How it works

- **10 meals a week for $129.** That's about $12.90 a meal, delivered every Sunday.
- **Choose what you eat.** The menu repeats every four weeks, and each week you can swap any meal for one of six other options.
- **Order by Thursday at noon** for that Sunday's delivery.
- **No contract.** Skip a week or cancel any time.

### People stay

Today, 88 people get their meals from Steady Plate. Of those, 37 have been with us for more than six months.

### Try one week first

Not sure yet? Start with a trial week for $59. You'll get your call with me and a week of meals. You can see whether Steady Plate fits your life before you sign up for the full plan.

**[Start your trial week: $59]**

*Steady Plate · Lena Ortiz, RD · Delivering within 25 miles of downtown*
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **What I left out:**
  - **Trial-to-plan rate:** I didn't use the 1-in-5 figure. It wouldn't persuade a buyer and might make some hesitate.
  - **Allergies and delivery window:** Once you know which allergies you can handle and when deliveries arrive, add both under "How it works." People will ask about them.
- **Check the trial week:** The page says the trial includes your call and "a week of meals." If the trial is fewer than 10 meals, say exactly what's included.
- **Add the link:** Both order buttons need it once you have the URL.
